canonical_answer: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is an evidence-based form of psychotherapy that helps people reduce the grip of difficult thoughts and feelings by changing their relationship to inner experience rather than trying to eliminate it. ACT uses mindfulness and values-based action to build psychological flexibility.

It is among the most extensively researched psychological treatments available and is effective for a wide range of mental health conditions.

It typically runs 12 sessions and does not require detailed retelling of traumatic events.
